pr_title: Allow AnimationStateMachine / AnimationNode to restart when transitioning to the same state
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5965
Fixed #69570
Fixed #69382
Fixed #71195

Allow AnimationStateMachine / AnimationNode to restart when transitioning to the same state. Also, allow NodeTransition to use String values.

Containing #71264. At first I was working with it as same PR #71264, but a few fundamental modifications caused break compatibility, so I separated this PR.

### StateMachine

Make it restart when it tries to travel() to the same state. This can be resolved with one line change.

### NodeTransition / NodeOneShot

For this, there was a problem with the original implementation, and 2 fundamental modifications are necessary.

1:
Currently they detect state changes by whether the property has changed from the previous frame, but this does not allow changes to the same state.

This means that they need an independent property as a request, like a StateMachine. So, implement the following properties for state changes.

**NodeTransition:**
```gdscript
# Property for the transition state requests. It will be cleared immediately in the next animation tree process.
anim_tree["parameters/TransitionNode/transition_request"] = "Input 2" # It is changed to String from int, to fix #69382.

# To avoid finding for an index every frame and to keep better performance, separate the following:
print(anim_tree["parameters/TransitionNode/current_state"]) # String value as state name for display. Read-only.
print(anim_tree["parameters/TransitionNode/current_index"]) # Int value as state index for internal use. Read-only.
```

**NodeOneShot:**
```gdscript
# Property for the transition state requests. It will be cleared immediately in the next animation tree process.
anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE
anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT

print(anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/active"]) # Read-only.
```

In addition, since there was only one `active` flag, there was no way to stop `auto restart` from the property, but now `auto restart` is stopped by an abort request.

2:
Some properties need to be changed only by request to prevent to make broken state, but the current status should be retrievable, so it should be PROPERTY_USAGE_READ_ONLY, not PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE.

However, the entity of the AnimationNode property is stored in the AnimationTree's map. During playback, the AnimationNode fetches the properties from the map, which means that read-only cannot be set using the USAGE flag.

Therefore, it is necessary to add a bool value to the AnimationTree map to implement read-only for the AnimationNode's parameter.

### Video

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/212488143-a2efedb0-3c8f-46b5-9a6e-20dc5dee2379.mp4

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/212488137-03b4e67b-0871-4d3b-9510-47ff6b7169e5.mp4

[restart_test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10419585/restart_test.zip)

If approved, I will update the document as soon as possible.
pr_comments:
@SaracenOne I get the feeling that "skip" is going to ignore xfade. So how about the following:
- step()
- forth()
- ahead()
- go_next()
For now, I renamed `interrupt()` to `next()`. Possibly, it could be mixed up with the List iterator on cpp, but for gdscript and general users, I guess it is no problem.
This looks mostly good to me, would be good to agree a proper name with @SaracenOne before merging

How do I trigger a Fire or Abort request on a OneShot node in the code??
I've tried AnimatrionTree.set("parameters/oneshotanim/request", "Fire") but it doesn't do anything...

It has been described in the description. The document(tutorial) for AnimationTree is overall out of date and needs to be updated later.

```gdscript
# Property for the transition state requests. It will be cleared immediately in the next animation tree process.
anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE
anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT

anim_tree.set("parameters/OneShotNode/request", AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE)
anim_tree.set("parameters/OneShotNode/request", AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT)

print(anim_tree["parameters/OneShotNode/active"]) # Read-only.
```

Why can't we just say "Fire" instead of AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE? This is making things more complicated. It's also inconsistent with Transitions where you can set the state parameter via a string...

Transition has a clear list of strings, but OneShot uses just an Enum as an Int for the request.
I don't know of any other method in Godot that allows a specific static const string to be input for a property instead of an Enum. If there is already such a method and it is allowed, I would consider some kind of binding.

Any way of checking if StateMachine is already in a given state so **not** to restart the animation when using travel() to the same state? Maybe the travel() function could have a second parameter (restart = true, false) to avoid restarting so to resemble the previous behavior. Or maybe is about documentation.

If there is a long crossfade, it may have already moved to the next state, and we may be better to expose the `fading_from`. It seems that cpp has a function `get_blend_from_node()`, but it is not bound and not exposed... I will send a PR.

There is also a second argument, reset_on_teleport, but if it is false, it would certainly make more sense not to restart with travel. I thought I had implemented it that way, but there seems to be some problem and it is not working. I will fix it later.

@jcarlosrc I sent #71840. With that, you can write:
```gdscript
state_machine_playback.travel("A", state_machine_playback.get_current_node() != "A")
```

It does not allow its own restart. But it allows teleports and resets from other states. Note just that the existing travel path is to be discarded. In order to keep the existing travel path, if statement must be used.

issue_context.title: AnimationStateMachine doesn't run consistently when animation entrance was spammed
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Official 4.0 beta 5 and 6

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Using AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer, using `Input.is_action_just_pressed` to then call `state_machine.travel("Roll")` which then plays the animation from a BlendTree2D with no issue if there is space between each call.

The Roll animations then have a Call Method track that calls a function. This also gets called consistently when there is space between the inputs.

But if you spam the input key, this function is sporadically not called. Same issue with Attack, which is set up the exact same way.

Perhaps related, perhaps not, but the `AnimationPlayer - animation_finished(string)` signal ALSO never seems to be called. I've specifically checked as per docs that none of the animations are set to loop, which would disable this signal.

Tested in b5 and b6 (6 has no animations playing due to known `RESET` bug, but the call method track still fails on input spam.)

Issue persists when changing `Method Call Mode` to any setting.

### Steps to reproduce

Open project, Run. Mopve around with WASD to set animation directions. Attempt to roll by pressing `F` Wait until roll is complete then `F` again to roll again. No issues.

Instead, spam the `F` key. Eventually it will not stop moving when it should (sliding to the edge) and other controls are unresponsive because you are in ROLL state. 

Check console during above, you will see "Start roll" from ENTERING the animation, but no "End Roll" from the Animation player's call method function on the spammed issue.

Same issue without console outputs if you use `Space` to do ATTACK animations instead.

### Minimal reproduction project

[HeartBeast ARPG - Copy.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10121854/HeartBeast.ARPG.-.Copy.zip)
comments:




the problem disappears.

Maybe I'm doing something wrong, my attempt to do MRP:
[spam_transition_test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10133495/spam_transition_test.zip)

(by the way, for tests I used build from #69336 to bypass #69415)

Running your upload project gets stuck in spin state EVERY time for me. (Running in official beta 5 though)

~~Moving the `state.travel` made no difference to my project or uploaded project.~~

~~Edit: Scratch that, misread where you said to move them. Yes, moving them to inside the state fixes it... That's.. odd.~~ 

1. ~~surely that's a sign of a problem?~~
2. Is that likely to cause issues, telling my state_machine to travel 15+ times because it's called every physics frame?

I've temporarily solved 2. by putting `	if(state_machine.get_current_node() != "Roll"):` before the travel, giving me the fix and in theory only running once.

Edit-edit, I don't believe the move fixes it, it masks it, as it fails to run `call method` track, and simply rolls again, and the next time works. It's mostly hidden by spamming the keys, but it is actually still failing.

> Running your upload project gets stuck in spin state EVERY time for me. (Running in official beta 5 though)

As I mentioned, for tests, I used build from #69336 to separate your problem from this one #69415. So if you want to test it, use build from [actions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/3592876308) or move method call away from the end of the animation.

> Is that likely to cause issues, telling my state_machine to travel 15+ times because it's called every physics frame?

I didn't suggest this as the correct fix. I just mentioned it in the hope that it will help you, or another person who decides to dive into this issue, find its cause.

> Edit-edit, I don't believe the move fixes it, it masks it, as it fails to run call method track, and simply rolls again, and the next time works. It's mostly hidden by spamming the keys, but it is actually still failing.

Perhaps.

--- 

**UPD:**

After some additional testing, I was able to reproduce the issue in my MRP. The error occurs if the `method call` time on the timeline is less than ≈0.4.

All of the following using the original problem project:

>As I mentioned, for tests, I used build from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69336 to separate your problem from this one https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69415. So if you want to test it, use build from [actions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/3592876308) or move method call away from the end of the animation.

I downloaded the linked build, using my original code the problem persists for me 

>After some additional testing, I was able to reproduce the issue in my MRP. The error occurs if the method call time on the timeline is less than ≈0.4.

I adjusted mine to a 1 second animation, with the method call at 0.8, and it still fails.

Are you sure that you test adjusted animation? You have 4 of them, 1 for each side. Try this:
[HeartBeast ARPG - Copy.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10137084/HeartBeast.ARPG.-.Copy.zip)

By the way, this is not a suggestion how to fix the problem. Just additional information that may be useful (or not) to those who undertake to fix it.


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10379487/205186673-8a010426-73ca-4984-adad-2464822b157a.mp4

(the animations look broken because of the wrong length, but I spam on the attack and roll keys.)

That project breaks for me in official beta 5 (it never ever calls the Call Method Track), and the animations are 0.4 long (Mine are normally 0.25)

In the custom build, you're right, `Call_Method` track works at 0.4 but does NOT work at 0.25

I tested back in 0.01 increments. 0.39 works, 0.38 does not. Can you confirm a boundary at that point?

That would also explain why no one in the comments of the tutorial I'm following has mentioned this: The projects instructions are for 0.4s long. It appears this should be a bug titled `Call Method track does not fire in first 0.38 seconds if spammed`
This time varies slightly, for example, depending on whether _process or _physics_process is used.  Also, depending on which node the transition occurs, Animation or BlendSpace2D, etc.

Maybe the problem is related to this issue #68986, but I don't know since I have not much knowledge about StateMachine.

I remember there is a plan to rework StateMachine, but I don't know detail. cc @SaracenOne

This issue is caused by the state on the GDScript and the StateMachine state being out of sync, and the StateMachine Node is trying to transition (restart) to itself, which is not yet supported. The following code would solve this problem.

```gdscript
	if (Input.is_action_just_pressed("Roll")):
		if (state != ROLL):
			print("Roll start")
			state = ROLL
			state_machine.travel("Roll")
```
↓
```gdscript
	if (Input.is_action_just_pressed("Roll")):
		if (state_machine.get_current_node() != "Roll"):
			print("Roll start")
			state = ROLL
			state_machine.travel("Roll")
```
That's very close to my current work around, better in terms of running too (just a minor reorganise of code, but mine runs the check more often currently).
